issue.title: Fix chunk hashes when sourcemaps add comments
issue.body:
This PR contains:

- [ ] feature
- [ ] refactor

- [ ] other

Are tests included?

### Description

Chunk content hashes were calculated before Rollup appended the sourceMappingURL comment. As a result, enabling a sourcemap could change the emitted JavaScript bytes without changing a hashed chunk file name.

issue.title: fix: match paths with unmatched double quotes
issue.body:
### What is the purpose of this pull request?

Fixes #494. A pattern such as `some/"path/*.txt` finds the correct base directory, but returns no entries when the literal directory name starts with a double quote.

Picomatch treats the unmatched quote as the start of a quoted expression, so the wildcard that follows it is compiled as a literal `*`. This only affects final pattern matching; traversal already reaches the quoted directory.

### What changes did you make? (Give an overview)

Escape an unmatched, unescaped double quote before compiling the pattern regex. Paired quotes and quotes already escaped by the caller retain their existing behavior.

Added unit coverage for the regex behavior and an end-to-end fixture covering sync, async, and stream APIs.

issue.title: fix(client): discard timed-out buffered packets
issue.body:
### The kind of change this PR does introduce

* [x] a bug fix
* [ ] a new feature
* [ ] an update to the documentation
* [ ] a code change that improves performance
* [ ] other

### Current behavior

An event with an acknowledgement timeout can already be queued in the Engine.IO write buffer when the transport becomes temporarily unwritable. The Socket.IO acknowledgement callback times out and the packet is removed from the Socket.IO send buffer, but the Engine.IO packet remains queued and is sent when the transport becomes writable again.

For binary events, one Socket.IO event can map to several Engine.IO packets.

### New behavior

When an acknowledgement times out, the client removes every Engine.IO packet created from that Socket.IO event if none of them has been handed to the transport yet.

If any encoded packet is already part of the current transport batch, all related packets are preserved so a binary event cannot be left partially transmitted.

### Other information (e.g. related issues)

Fixes #4318.

Tests cover both multi-packet binary events and the partially-flushed safety boundary.

Verification:

- Engine.IO client formatting and TypeScript compilation
- Socket.IO client formatting and TypeScript compilation
- Engine.IO buffer-removal regression tests
- Socket.IO timeout tests (20 passing)

issue.body:
## Summary

- emit a transport error when an HTTP polling payload exceeds `maxHttpBufferSize`
- preserve the existing HTTP 413 response
- assert that server-side close handlers receive an actionable `TransportError`

## Context

The polling transport returned HTTP 413 when the incoming body crossed the configured limit, but it did not notify the Engine.IO socket about the cause. As a result, server-side Socket.IO handlers only received `transport close` without a description.

The uWebSockets polling implementation already reports `payload too large`, and the WebSocket implementation reports the corresponding `ws` range error. This change brings the Node.js polling transport in line with those paths by using the existing transport error pipeline after the request has been cleaned up.

issue.title: fix: preserve dot segments in request paths
issue.body:
Fixes #1816.

## What changed

- Protect literal and percent-encoded dot-only path segments while the URL components are parsed with the WHATWG `URL` API.
- Restore those segments when constructing the path passed to Node's HTTP client.
- Add a regression test that checks the exact outgoing request path.

## Why

The migration from `url.parse()` to `new URL()` in 9.0.2 made request paths go through WHATWG dot-segment normalization. That silently changed paths such as `/api/v2/../error` to `/api/error` before they were sent.

The fix keeps WHATWG parsing for protocol, host, credentials, encoding, and query handling; only path segments that would otherwise be collapsed are temporarily protected and restored.

issue.title: fix: allow passthrough requests with large headers
issue.body:
Fixes #3002

## Problem

`@mswjs/interceptors@0.41` parses outgoing request headers with Node's default incoming-header limit. A larger header returns `HPE_HEADER_OVERFLOW` before the request reaches Nock's request handler, and that parser result is ignored, leaving the request pending forever instead of passing it through to the server.

## Fix

Raise the interceptor-owned outgoing parser limit when its socket is assigned to `ClientRequest`. Native sockets are left untouched, and the original `onSocket` method is restored when Nock is deactivated. This keeps the current Node 18/20 support without upgrading to the Node 22-only interceptor release.

## Test

issue.title: fix(shell): preserve argument boundaries when expanding $@
issue.body:
## What's the problem this PR addresses?

Closes #6968.

The portable shell loses positional-argument boundaries when expanding unquoted `$@`: the final field from one positional argument remains open and is concatenated with the next one. Quoted `$@` has the inverse edge case, closing every field too early so a suffix becomes a separate argument instead of attaching to the final positional argument.

## How did you fix it?

Both forms now produce a single field list—preserving quoted values or applying field splitting when unquoted—and close only the fields before the final one. This keeps each positional argument separate while allowing surrounding text to attach to the first and last fields as shell expansion requires.

Regression tests cover quoted and unquoted expansion, adjacent prefixes and suffixes, whitespace splitting, empty positional arguments, and the zero-argument case.

Validation:

issue.title: fix: match paths with unmatched double quotes
issue.body:
### What is the purpose of this pull request?

Fixes #494. A pattern such as `some/"path/*.txt` finds the correct base directory, but returns no entries when the literal directory name starts with a double quote.

Picomatch treats the unmatched quote as the start of a quoted expression, so the wildcard that follows it is compiled as a literal `*`. This only affects final pattern matching; traversal already reaches the quoted directory.

### What changes did you make? (Give an overview)

Escape an unmatched, unescaped double quote before compiling the pattern regex. Paired quotes and quotes already escaped by the caller retain their existing behavior.

Added unit coverage for the regex behavior and an end-to-end fixture covering sync, async, and stream APIs.

Validation:

- `npm run build` — TypeScript, ESLint, and 268 unit tests passed
- `npm run test:e2e` — 1374 passed, 9 platform-specific tests pending

comment.body:
You are right to question the layer. After isolating it further, the same failure reproduces directly in the matchers, without any fast-glob traversal:

```js
const pattern = `root/"directory/*.js`
const value = `root/"directory/index.js`

micromatch([value], pattern) // []
picomatch(pattern)(value)    // false
```

I verified this with micromatch 4.0.8 / picomatch 2.3.2 and picomatch 4.0.7. The generated regex drops the literal quote and treats the following `*` literally. fast-glob already derives the correct base directory and reaches the entry; the miss only happens in the final matcher regex.

I initially kept the workaround here because the reported contract is matching a real filesystem name containing a literal quote, and a local normalization limits the compatibility surface while preserving paired and explicitly escaped quote behavior. But given the direct upstream reproduction, I agree that the canonical parser fix belongs in picomatch (and then reaches micromatch).

Would you prefer that I move the fix upstream and then reduce this PR to regression coverage / the corresponding dependency update once an upstream release is available?

issue.title: fix(core): use scoped config form for pnpm 11+ publish
issue.body:
## Current Behavior

Nx uses the direct scoped registry option for every pnpm version from 10.5.0 onward. pnpm 12 rejects that option, while falling back to the plain registry option can let a scoped registry in .npmrc win and silently publish to the wrong registry.

## Expected Behavior

Nx keeps the direct scoped option for supported pnpm 9/10 releases and uses the config-prefixed scoped option for pnpm 11 and newer, so an explicit release registry overrides workspace configuration.

## Tests

- pnpm exec vitest --config packages/nx/vitest.config.mts run packages/nx/src/utils/package-manager.spec.ts (106 tests)
- pnpm exec tsc -p packages/nx/tsconfig.lib.json --noEmit
- npx oxfmt packages/nx/src/utils/package-manager.ts packages/nx/src/utils/package-manager.spec.ts

## Related Issue(s)

Fixes #36860

issue.title: Not calling next on io.of('/test') middleware does not timeout or error

comment.body:
I checked this against the current `main` branch (Socket.IO 4.8.3). The server-wide `connectTimeout` now covers this case: if namespace middleware never calls `next()`, no namespace is joined, and the underlying client connection is closed when that timeout expires (45 seconds by default).

I reproduced the exact middleware pattern with `connectTimeout: 10` and a regression test observing the client `disconnect` event; it passes locally. There is also an existing nearby test for a client that never sends a namespace CONNECT packet.

So the connection no longer remains open forever on current main. If the desired behavior is specifically a `connect_error` packet (rather than transport disconnection) or a separate per-middleware timeout, that would be an API/design change; confirmation of the intended behavior would be useful before preparing a patch.

issue.title: [Bug]: sharded pubsub uses wrong channel after joining a room with namespace

comment.body:
I investigated this on the current `main` branch. The channel selection shown in the report is expected for `subscriptionMode: "dynamic"`:

- every adapter stays subscribed to the namespace base channel (`...#/adasd#`)
- public rooms such as `Room 1` get an additional dynamic subscription
- a socket ID is a private room, so `ns.to(socket.id)` publishes on the base channel in `dynamic` mode; `dynamic-private` is the mode that creates a dedicated channel for private rooms

I also ran the Redis 5 sharded-adapter tests with three Socket.IO servers. Both the public-room broadcast and `broadcasts to a single client` pass in dynamic mode. The `Room 1` subscription in the log does not replace the base subscription.

If delivery still fails on a current release, could you share the adapter version and a minimal two-server reproduction? In particular, logs for the initial base-channel subscriptions would help distinguish a subscription/setup failure from channel selection.

issue.title: Static error overrides are shared across validations

labels.name: repo-0aacc98c
labels.description: Issue is not a problem or requires changes

issue.body:
### Runtime

Node.js

### Runtime version

22.14.0

### Module version

18.2.5

### Last module version without issue

_No response_

### Used with

@hapi/hapi

### Any other relevant information

This is the Joi-side cause identified in hapijs/hapi#4582. Hapi decorates validation errors, so reusing the same override can leak request-specific data into later validations.

AI assistance disclosure: OpenAI Codex assisted with the investigation and drafting. The reproduction and the full Joi test suite were run locally.

### What are you trying to achieve or the steps to reproduce?

A static error passed to `any.error()` is returned by reference on every validation:

```js
const Joi = require('joi');

const override = new Error('shared');
override.data = { owner: 'original' };

const schema = Joi.any().invalid('x').error(override);
const first = schema.validate('x').error;
first.data.request = 'first';

const second = schema.validate('x').error;

console.log(first === second);        // true
console.log(second.data.request);    // 'first'
console.log(override.data.request);  // 'first'
```

### What was the result you got?

The schema, every validation result, and downstream consumers share one mutable Error object. A consumer decorating one validation error changes the configured override and every later result. With concurrent requests, request-specific error data can be overwritten by another request.

### What result did you expect?

Each validation should receive an isolated Error that retains the configured error prototype and properties without mutating the configured override.

A focused fix can clone only a directly configured static Error in the validation finalization path. This changes the documented object-identity behavior of `any.error(error)`, so I would like confirmation that this direction is acceptable before opening the PR.
